<reason>CON won a close, high-quality clash by taking PRO’s irreversibility test and inverting it: a foreign scanner is a maintained, service-dependent state, while a ban-created domestic tool order book is the permanent loss of leverage. PRO’s factory-lock story and tutor/kill-switch attack were sharp, but CON better showed the motion’s delay was unnamed and possibly self-defeating, and resolved the mature-node versus lithography tension with the “ladder” dilemma.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON Rebuttal 2: either the frontier matters, so funding the indigenous tool stack is the worst outcome, or it doesn’t, so the ban buys nothing—then weighing that against PRO’s unnamed delay.</best_rebuttal>
